10.1002_adfm.76917: Lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs) using a Li anode and nickel (Ni)‐rich cathode constitute a promising powering solution for long‐range electric vehicles. Unfortunately, both the Li anode and Ni‐rich cathode suffer from surface deterioration‐related failures. Herein, an ionic complex‐anchored interlayer consisting of positively charged skeletons with conjugated π bonds, Li + ions, and functional anions is investigated to trigger a cross‐linked surface chemistry regulation in LMBs. It is revealed that the Li + and anions electrostatically anchored on the interlayer can be released to alter the crossover electrochemistry of LMB for durable electrode interphases. Furthermore, by presetting the interlayer on a carbonaceous scaffold, an extended delocalization path of π electrons enables uniform adsorption of the anions, while the prelithiated carbon scaffold by Li + from the interlayer facilitates the anion decomposition to form a robust bilayer surface, affording reversible Li plating/stripping with high average coulombic efficiency beyond 99.5% over 500 cycles. Simultaneously, the modified cathode interphase withstands structural stability of the Ni‐rich materials and mitigates current collector corrosion efficiently. These merits lead to significantly enhanced performance of LMBs, where stable cycling over 150 cycles is achieved for an anode‐free pouch cell with a high cathode loading of 6 mAh cm −2 .
10.1016_j.electacta.2026.148668: We present an innovative electrochemical sensing method for the detection of heavy metal cations that departs from conventional pulsed electroanalytical techniques. The keystone of this approach is the nanostructuring of trace amounts of preconcentrated metal on a functionalized electrode, thereby exploiting the heterogeneous catalytic properties of the resulting metal nanodeposits. Rather than introducing a new selective sensing interface, this work focuses on a general detection strategy. In this approach, a diazonium modified graphite electrode is used as a robust platform to demonstrate that sparsely pre accumulated metal cations can be reduced into nanodeposits, which behave as a nanoelectrode array. The macroscopic electrochemical response of this array towards the hydrogen evolution reaction depends on the size of the nanoelectrodes: higher metal concentrations in the incubation solution lead to more extensive metal deposition and larger nanostructures, which shift the hydrogen evolution reaction catalytic peak potential positively in cyclic voltammetry. This shift continues until the metal becomes detectable by standard pulsed analytical methods. As an illustration, the proposed approach enables the detection of copper and iron with improved sensitivity compared to the corresponding reference pulsed techniques. Moreover, this gain in sensitivity does not rely on a specific surface chemistry. Therefore, the more affine a given accumulation layer is for its target metal, the lower the detection limits that can be achieved with this method. This study points toward a promising route for next generation electrochemical sensors for trace metal detection, offering sensitivity beyond that of traditional faradaic detection schemes.
10.1016_j.est.2026.123506: At present, flexible, wearable and implantable electronic devices (FWIEDs), renewable energy (RE) systems and Net Zero platforms are predominantly powered by rechargeable batteries (RBs) specifically lithium-ion batteries (LiBs). This can potentially limit advancements of these systems in terms of cyclability, miniaturization and flexibility. In addition, RBs contain sizable quantities of toxic and flammable active materials posing threat to human health when used in some of the above cited applications. Therefore, it is vital to investigate innovative energy materials, design and experiment new devices to fulfil power requirements of current and prospective applications. This review discusses the fundamentals, followed by conventional and state of the art low-dimensional active materials and finally, market potential of flexible supercapacitors (FSCs). Pivotal segment of this study is the extensive level of emphasis on the existing and potential applications of FSCs including implantable medical devices, wearable electronics, soft robotics, Internet of Things/Everything and RE/Net Zero platforms. Finally, insights are provided of the challenges presently faced by FSCs for broader commercialisation and outlook in the form of potential as energy storage devices (ESDs) in next generation applications in short, medium and long term.
10.1016_j.polymer.2026.130557: Scale deposition and corrosion remain critical challenges in oilfield operations, often leading to equipment deterioration and reduced production efficiency. Conventional inhibitors, though effective, suffer from poor biodegradability and environmental concerns, necessitating greener alternatives. In this study, we report the synthesis of phosphonated polyaminopropyl biguanide (PPAPB) via the Moedritzer-Irani reaction, introducing phosphonate groups into the polyaminopropyl biguanide (PAPB) backbone to yield a dual-function inhibitor. The structural characterization was carried out by NMR, FTIR and XPS spectroscopy, which confirmed the successful incorporation of phosphonate groups into PAPB, and the degree of substitution (DS) determined by NMR validated this phosphonation functionalization process. PPAPB demonstrated excellent scale inhibition against calcium carbonate and calcium sulfate under NACE static bottle test conditions, achieving complete suppression of gypsum scale at 5 ppm and maintaining high efficiency after thermal aging at 130 °C for one week. Compatibility tests confirmed stability in brines containing up to 10,000 ppm Ca 2+ . Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed superior corrosion resistance compared to the commercial inhibitor NABMP. PPAPB forms a protective chemisorbed monolayer on carbon steel surfaces, and its adsorption behaviour conforms to the Langmuir isotherm, showing strong and specific surface interactions. These findings highlight PPAPB as a sustainable, environmentally acceptable, and highly efficient scale and corrosion inhibitor for demanding oilfield applications.
10.1021_acsami.5c26162: Nonaqueous organic redox flow batteries (NAORFBs) are desirable candidates for large-scale energy storage applications. 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidin-1-oxyl (TEMPO) derivatives exhibit favorable electrochemical activity, but their practical applications are severely constrained by their instability. Functional group modifications are essential for regulating the redox potential, solubility, and chemical and electrochemical stability. Herein, we propose a biomimetic molecular engineering strategy to synthesize 4-[2-(diethoxyphosphoryl)­acetamino]-2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (DEPAcNH-TEMPO) modified with amide bonds and diethyl phosphate groups in a one-step route. DEPAcNH-TEMPO has high solubility (1.8 M), excellent electrokinetic properties, and impressive stability. When paired with 1,1′-dibenzyl-4,4′-bipyridinediium dihexafluoro-phosphate (DBV), the DEPAcNH-TEMPO/DBV NAORFB exhibits superior rate performance and improves cycling stability by nearly 20 times compared to unmodified 4-NH2-TEMPO. These results highlight the importance of rational biomimetic design in suppressing molecular degradation and provide useful guidance for the development of stable, high-performance catholytes for next-generation NAORFBs.
10.1021_acsnano.5c13246: Efficient hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in alkaline and neutral media remains a major challenge due to sluggish water dissociation and limited proton availability. Hydrogen spillover presents a promising strategy to couple proton generation and utilization; yet, its application in single-component catalysts is greatly limited by the absence of effective driving forces for hydrogen migration. Herein, we report an amino-functionalized NiRu-based metal–organic framework (MOF) as a single-component catalyst, wherein spontaneously formed frustrated Lewis pairs (FLPs) composed of Ni sites and amino groups function as cooperative active sites to drive coupled water dissociation and hydrogen spillover, establishing a continuous short-range spillover pathway. Experimental and theoretical results reveal that Ni-NH 2 FLPs promote water adsorption and dissociation, generating a locally acidic microenvironment conducive to proton transport. Meanwhile, the amino groups modulate the electronic structure of neighboring Ru sites, lowering the energy barrier for hydrogen desorption and promoting spillover-mediated hydrogen release. As a result, the catalyst achieves Pt-beyond HER activity and durability under alkaline and neutral conditions at industrial current densities. The assembled alkaline electrolyzer further demonstrates a low cell voltage (1.76 V at 0.5 A cm –2 ), high energy efficiency (71.2%), and hydrogen production cost ($0.94 per GGE) below the U.S. Department of Energy target.
